Seminar Title:

Development and Evaluation of a Yoga-Based Intervention Program to Enhance Psychological Immunity and Positive Psychological Outcomes among Central Armed Police Forces in India

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Humanities and Social Sciences

Speaker Name:

Aarsh Ojas Parasar Pandey ( Rollno : 519hs1006)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

HS Seminar Room (MN 436)

Date and Time:

03 Jul 2026 10:00 AM

Contact:

Koteswara Rao Kodirekkala

Abstract:

Background:&nbspCentral Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel frequently operate in challenging and high-stress environments that require not only physical preparedness but also sustained psychological resilience and emotional stability. In such contexts, positive psychological resources, such as psychological immunity, self-efficacy, happiness, and life satisfaction, become highly relevant to healthy adjustment and effective functioning. Yoga, as a holistic mind-body discipline, has increasingly been recognised as a promising intervention for improving overall well-being, yet its structured application for strengthening positive psychological capacities among CAPF personnel remains limited. The present study addressed this gap and was designed to develop a yoga-based intervention targeting psychological immunity and broader well-being outcomes among Central Reserve Police Forces (CRPF) Personnel, a specialised unit of CAPF.

Objectives/Purpose:&nbspThe study aimed to develop and evaluate a yoga-based intervention to enhance psychological immunity and positive psychological outcomes among CRPF personnel. More specifically, it sought to examine whether the intervention could significantly enhance psychological immunity, self-efficacy, happiness, and life satisfaction among participants exposed to the program.

Methods:&nbspThe study employed a pretest-posttest control group design in order to assess the effectiveness of the intervention among CRPF Personnel. We screened 50 participants for this study, of whom 40 (Mage = 33.62 &plusmn 4.12) were included in the final analysis. Participants were randomly assigned to an experimental (yoga) group and a control group, and a baseline assessment of the major outcome variables was conducted before the intervention. Psycho-Immunity Scale (PIS), Self-Efficacy Scale (SES), Happiness Scale (HS), and Life Satisfaction Scale (LSS) were used to assess participants&rsquo psychological immunity, self-efficacy, happiness, and life satisfaction, respectively. The experimental group received the yoga-based intervention program developed for the study, administered six days a week for one month. The control group did not participate in the intervention or other such activities during the same period. Following the intervention, a post-assessment was conducted to examine changes in outcome variables. This design enabled the study to evaluate the efficacy of yoga-based intervention by comparing pre- and post-intervention changes across groups.

Results:&nbspThe findings indicated that the yoga-based intervention produced significant positive changes in the psychological functioning of the participants. The experimental group demonstrated significant improvements in psychological immunity (p &lt 0.01), self-efficacy (p &lt 0.01), happiness (p &lt 0.01), and life satisfaction (p &lt 0.01), supporting the usefulness of yoga as a structured psychological resource in CAPF settings. In contrast, no such changes were obtained in the control group participants.&nbsp

Conclusion:&nbspThe study concludes that a yoga-based intervention can serve as a meaningful and culturally relevant approach for enhancing psychological immunity, self-efficacy, happiness, and life satisfaction among CAPF personnel. By integrating yogic practices into psychological support strategies, it may be possible to strengthen adaptive capacities and promote healthier psychological functioning in demanding occupational environments.

Keywords: Psychological Immunity, Self-Efficacy, Happiness, Life Satisfaction, Yoga, Armed Forces, Positive Psychology.
